claims.text: Selective isotopic substitution in refractory-element HEA nanoparticles increases vibrational entropy.
Increasing vibrational entropy lowers the free-energy barrier for surface-atom mobilization.
A lower barrier for surface-atom mobilization causes premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
Isotopic substitution can modify lattice vibrational properties while leaving the elemental composition unchanged.
Isotopic substitution can be implemented while keeping the atomic-size distribution constant.
Isotopic substitution alters lattice dynamics and redistributes vibrational entropy.
The modified vibrational-entropy distribution reduces the free-energy barrier for surface and subsurface atomic mobilization.
Enhanced lattice vibrational activity facilitates earlier initiation of premelting.
Isotopically substituted nanoparticles will have a statistically significant lower premelting-onset temperature than naturally isotopic nanoparticles.
The lower premelting onset will produce a shift in the DSC endothermic peak.
The lower premelting onset will be accompanied by TEM-observable surface disorder.
The proposed relationship should hold for refractory-element HEA nanoparticles approximately 7 nm in diameter.
The premelting-temperature shift may be subtle enough to be obscured by experimental noise.
